title: Due Date Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Due Date Calculator: Estimated due date from last period. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.
content:
The [Due Date Calculator](/due-date-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Estimated due date from last period. Enter your first day of last period and cycle length and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Your due date is estimated as 40 weeks (280 days) from the first day of your last menstrual period, adjusted for cycle length. Only about 4% of babies arrive on the exact day. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Pregnancy tools include [Pregnancy Calculator](/pregnancy-calculator), [Ovulation Calculator](/ovulation-calculator) and [Pregnancy Weight Gain Calculator](/pregnancy-weight-gain-calculator).

## How to use the Due Date Calculator

Start by picking your first day of last period, then entering your cycle length (days). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Pick your first day of last period.
2. Enter your cycle length (days).
3. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
4. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

Naegele's rule: LMP + 280 days, ± (cycle length − 28).

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Due Date Calculator](/due-date-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. If your last period began on 1 March 2026 with a 28-day cycle, your due date is 6 December 2026. Try the same figures in the [Due Date Calculator](/due-date-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (First day of last period: 2026-03-01, Cycle length: 28 days), the [Due Date Calculator](/due-date-calculator) returns Estimated due date: Sun, December 6, 2026, Estimated conception: Sun, March 15, 2026, End of first trimester: Sun, May 31, 2026. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. ## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- An early ultrasound gives the most accurate dating.
- Full term is 39–40 weeks.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### How accurate is a due date?

Most babies are born within two weeks either side of the estimated date. For figures that matter, such as money, health or legal deadlines, check the result against an authoritative source before acting on it.

### What if my cycle is irregular?

An ultrasound in the first trimester is more reliable than LMP-based dating. Try it with your own numbers in the [Due Date Calculator](/due-date-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Due Date Calculator use?

Naegele's rule: LMP + 280 days, ± (cycle length − 28). You can see it in action in the [Due Date Calculator](/due-date-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Due Date Calculator?

Just First day of last period and Cycle length. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
